headwords: trông lên thì chẳng bằng ai, trông xuống thì cũng chẳng ai bằng mình

flags.why: The entry omits the everyday meaning ‘to climb a tree’.
flags.fix: Add: verb | to climb a tree; ex: Hồi nhỏ, tôi thích trèo cây. = As a child, I liked climbing trees.

flags.why: A learner will encounter tree climbing much more often than the bird name.
flags.fix: Put ‘to climb a tree’ first and the nuthatch sense second.

flags.why: Calling someone trì độn disparages their intelligence and requires a derogatory warning.
The word means slow and dull-witted, not careful or thoughtful before speaking, as confirmed by [the dictionary definition](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/tr%C3%AC_%C4%91%E1%BB%99n).
Ánh mắt ông trí lự unnaturally uses a noun for thoughts or deliberation as an adjective, contrary to [the dictionary definition](https://home.vndic.net/tr%C3%AD%20l%E1%BB%B1-vi_vi.html).
flags.fix: Remove the adjective sense and its example.

flags.headword: trông lên thì chẳng bằng ai, trông xuống thì cũng chẳng ai bằng mình
flags.why: The proverb encourages perspective and contentment by comparing one's circumstances with those better and worse off, as illustrated in [this educational text](https://c12binhchuong-binhchuong.quangngai.edu.vn/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/8.-Sach-Hieu-truong-nguoi-gieo-mam-hanh-phuc.pdf).
flags.fix: Others are better off than you, but others are worse off too; be content with what you have.
